newsitem.title: USA: Republicans praise public housing bill.
newsitem.headline: Republicans praise public housing bill.

text.p: Congressional Republicans Saturday said a bill to overhaul the public housing program and open up apartments to more of the working poor would create greater self-sufficiency among low-income Americans.
The bill cleared the House Wednesday. "Working Americans won a great victory in the House of Representatives," Rep. Rick Lazio, R-N.Y., said in the weekly Republican radio address.
"The reality of public housing today as a warehouse for the poor came face-to-face with the promise of public housing tomorrow as a stepping stone to self-sufficiency."
But the Clinton administration and many Democrats charge the legislation would throw the very poor out of public housing in favor of moderate-income residents.

"The House bill adds insult to injury -- it seeks to improve public housing by excluding poor people and increasing public housing eligibility for people making $35,000 per year," Department of Housing and Urban Development Secretary Andrew Cuomo said in a statement.
Cuomo said he would urge President Clinton to veto the legislation if the House version reached his desk.

The bill, which would scrap the landmark Housing Act of 1937, would end many federal rules and is meant to give local housing authorities more power and leeway to run the nation's 13,200 public housing developments. Also, unemployed tenants would have to perform community service without pay.

"This is about restoring mixed-income neighborhoods where working families serve as role models," said Lazio, who spearheaded the bill. A less deregulatory version is pending in the Senate and is more to the administration's liking.
